crossRefs.note: Though he heap up silver as the dust, and prepare clothing as the clay;
he may prepare it, but the just will put it on, and the innocent will divide the silver.
“Surely every man walks like a shadow. Surely they busy themselves in vain. He heaps up, and doesn’t know who shall…
Those who trust in their wealth, and boast in the multitude of their riches—
A good man leaves an inheritance to his children’s children, but the wealth of the sinner is stored for the righteous.
He who increases his wealth by excessive interest gathers it for one who has pity on the poor.
I hated all my labor in which I labored under the sun, because I must leave it to the man who comes after me.
Who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? Yet he will have rule over all of my labor in which I have labored…

people.name: Ahasuerus
people.line: Persian Emperor (probably Xerxes I); husband of Esther

people.name: Esther
people.line: Jewish queen of Persia; saved her people from genocide.

people.name: Haman
people.line: A Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.

people.name: Mordecai
people.line: Esther's cousin, a Jewish leader in the Persian court.

translations.web: On that day, King Ahasuerus gave the house of Haman, the Jews’ enemy, to Esther the queen. Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was to her.
translations.bsb: That same day King Xerxes awarded Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai entered the king’s presence because Esther had revealed his relation to her.
